Definition: Word, message, reason and account — God's self-expression, culminating in Jesus Christ, the Word made flesh.
BiblicalUsage: Logos carried rich meaning for Jews (God's creative word) and Greeks (the reason ordering the universe). John seizes both: the Logos was God, was with God, and became flesh in Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: Logos declares that God has spoken — finally and personally — in His Son. We do not guess at God's heart; we look at Jesus, the Word made flesh.
RelatedTopics: Jesus Christ; Word of God; Incarnation
